s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic multisystem disorder with skin manifestations and endocrine abnormalities
salient_findings: Numerous asymptomatic reddish-brownish papules, nodules, and plaques over the whole body
Central diabetes insipidus, growth retardation, and hypothyroidism
key_facts: 7-year medical history of skin lesions
Skin lesions began on bilateral eyelid margins and extended to trunk and extremities
Patient has central diabetes insipidus
Patient has growth retardation
Patient has hypothyroidism
Skin biopsy showed dense granulomatous infiltrate in the upper dermis
Immunohistochemical results were negative for CD1a and S-100, positive for CD68

Skin lesions are present on periocular areas, perioral areas, neck, shoulder, axillary folds, cubital fossa, wrists, palms, umbilical region, lateral abdomen, inguinal area, anogenital area, popliteal fossa, and ankles

shortlist.label: Erdheim-Chester Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Matches chronic multisystem disorder with skin manifestations and endocrine abnormalities, and specific findings of granulomatous infiltrate and positive CD68

shortlist.label: Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with skin lesions, diabetes insipidus, and growth retardation, although immunohistochemical results were negative for CD1a and S-100

shortlist.label: Necrobiotic Xanthogranuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by granulomatous skin lesions and potential systemic involvement, including endocrine abnormalities

shortlist.label: Adult-Onset Multisystem Histocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Presents with multisystem involvement, including skin lesions and potential endocrine abnormalities, and histiocytic infiltrate

shortlist.label: Multifocal Eosinophilic Granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Involves skin lesions and potential systemic findings, including endocrine abnormalities, with histiocytic and eosinophilic infiltrate

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of numerous asymptomatic reddish-brownish papules, nodules, and plaques, along with central diabetes insipidus, growth retardation, and hypothyroidism, is consistent with Erdheim-Chester Disease, a rare form of non-Langerhans cell histiocytosis that can involve multiple systems and has been associated with various endocrine abnormalities.

rejected.label: Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
rejected.why: Immunohistochemical results were negative for CD1a and S-100, which are typically positive in Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis

rejected.label: Necrobiotic Xanthogranuloma
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and biopsy findings do not match those typically seen in Necrobiotic Xanthogranuloma, which often involves the periorbital area and has a distinct histological appearance

rejected.label: Adult-Onset Multisystem Histocytosis
rejected.why: While this condition involves multiple systems, the specific constellation of findings and the immunohistochemical results in this case are more consistent with Erdheim-Chester Disease

rejected.label: Multifocal Eosinophilic Granuloma
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with solitary or a few bone lesions and does not usually involve the widespread skin and systemic manifestations seen in this patient

rejected.label: Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia Type 1
rejected.why: While the patient has multiple endocrine abnormalities, the presence of skin lesions and the specific immunohistochemical profile are not typical of Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia Type 1
